name: John Sulston
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; completed BA (1963, age 21) and PhD (1966, age 24) at Cambridge, then postdoctoral fellowship at Salk Institute (1966-69). His landmark C. elegans cell lineage work began in 1969 at age 27.
evidence_summary: Sulston earned his BA from Cambridge in 1963 and PhD in 1966, followed by a postdoctoral fellowship at the Salk Institute. His Nobel Prize-winning work on C. elegans cell lineage did not begin until he joined Sydney Brenner's group at the MRC LMB in 1969, at age 27. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Charlton Heston
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Broadway debut in 1948 at age 24 in a revival of Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra starring Katharine Cornell, and appeared in leading roles on live television (CBS Studio One) before age 26.
early_history_summary: Heston acted in high school plays and appeared in an amateur film (Peer Gynt, 1941) at age 18. He earned a drama scholarship to Northwestern University (1941-43) but dropped out to serve in WWII. After the war, he managed a playhouse in Asheville, NC before returning to New York in 1948 for his Broadway debut.
family_context_summary: Father was a sawmill operator; parents divorced when Heston was 10. He grew up in rural Michigan before moving to the Chicago suburb of Wilmette. Modest middle-class background; he earned a scholarship to Northwestern.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family connections to acting or entertainment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: drama scholarship, Northwestern University, Broadway, post-war television boom
evidence_summary: Heston began acting in high school and appeared in an amateur film at 18. He studied drama at Northwestern on scholarship before WWII service. After the war, he made his Broadway debut at 24 in Antony and Cleopatra with Katharine Cornell and became a regular on CBS Studio One. His first professional film lead (Dark City) came at 26. Family background was modest with no entertainment connections; his advantage came from institutional training and the post-war New York theater/television boom.

name: Dave Murray
milestone_by_age_26: As a founding member of Iron Maiden, played on the band's self-titled debut album (1980, UK #4) and follow-up Killers (1981) by age 24, with The Number of the Beast (1982) following by age 25.
early_history_summary: Murray grew up in poverty in London, constantly moving schools. He discovered rock music at 15 after hearing Jimi Hendrix, left school at 16, and practiced guitar obsessively (up to 7 hours/day). He formed his first band Stone Free with Adrian Smith, then joined Iron Maiden in 1976 at age 19-20, remaining (except a brief hiatus) to the present.
primary_leverage_engine: Obsessive practice and early band membership
family_context_summary: Grew up in poverty; father retired early due to debilitating health condition, mother worked part-time as a cleaner. Family moved constantly around London's East End, attending over a dozen schools.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no family connections to music.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, London rock scene, NWOBHM, Steve Harris partnership, obsessive practice
evidence_summary: Murray grew up in deep poverty in London with a disabled father and cleaner mother, attending over a dozen schools. He discovered guitar at 15 after hearing Hendrix, left school at 16, and practiced obsessively. He joined Iron Maiden at 19-20 and played on their debut album (1980) at 23, which reached #4 in the UK. His advantages were the London rock ecosystem, the NWOBHM wave, and his partnership with Steve Harris, all set against a background of significant adversity.

name: Yoichiro Nambu
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; received BS from University of Tokyo in 1942 (age 21), then served in the Imperial Japanese Army. By 26 (1947), he was beginning postwar research but had not yet published notable work. His associate professorship at Osaka City University came in 1950 (age 29).
evidence_summary: Nambu received his BS from the University of Tokyo in 1942 and was immediately drafted into the Imperial Japanese Army. After the war, he began research but his first notable publications came around 1950 when he became an associate professor at Osaka City University (age 29). His Nobel Prize-winning work on spontaneous symmetry breaking was done in the 1960s. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Dieter Bohlen
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; studied business administration (graduated 1978), worked as a songwriter at Intersong/Hansa labels from 1979, but released only unsuccessful singles under pseudonyms. His breakthrough came with Modern Talking in 1984-85 at age 30-31.
family_context_summary: Father was a building contractor; family lived in East Frisia and later Oldenburg, Germany.
evidence_summary: Bohlen studied business administration and graduated in 1978. He began working as a songwriter at Intersong in Hamburg in 1979 (age 25) and later at Hansa label in 1980, releasing unsuccessful singles under pseudonyms like Steve Benson. His first hit came with Modern Talking's 'You're My Heart, You're My Soul' in 1985 at age 31. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Richard R. Ernst
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; completed diploma in chemistry at ETH Zurich in 1956 (age 23), did military service 1956-57, then began graduate studies. His PhD was completed in 1962 (age 29) and his groundbreaking Fourier NMR work at Varian Associates began in 1963 (age 30).
family_context_summary: Father was an architect teaching at the technical high school in Winterthur; family lived in a home built by his grandfather, a merchant. Middle-class background in a town with both artistic and industrial activities.
parent_family_domain_summary: An uncle who died in 1923 was a metallurgical engineer interested in chemistry and photography; Ernst found his chemicals in the attic at age 13, sparking his chemistry interest.
evidence_summary: Ernst completed his chemistry diploma at ETH Zurich in 1956 (age 23), followed by military service and then graduate studies. His PhD was awarded in 1962 (age 29) and his Nobel Prize-winning Fourier NMR work began at Varian Associates in 1963 (age 30). By age 26 he was a graduate student with no material milestone. His father was an architect and an uncle's chemistry set sparked his early interest.

name: Kakuichi Mimura
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for the Japan national football team on 2 January 1955 at age 23, playing four international matches that year, and was selected to represent Japan at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics.
early_history_summary: Mimura took up football after World War II as a high school student at Tokyo Daihachi High School, continuing at Chuo University. Upon graduation in 1955, he founded the Toho Titanium football club and immediately debuted for the Japan national team, playing four internationals against Burma in January 1955.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Tokyo Daihachi High School, Chuo University, Japan national team, post-war rebuilding
evidence_summary: Mimura took up football as a high school student in post-war Tokyo, playing at Tokyo Daihachi High School and Chuo University. Upon graduation in 1955 at age 23, he founded the Toho Titanium club and immediately debuted for the Japan national team on 2 January 1955, playing four internationals that year. He was selected for the 1956 Melbourne Olympics. Family background is not documented. His advantage came from the university football pipeline in post-war Japan.

name: Jean-Marie Lehn
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; earned Licence ès-Sciences (1960, age 21), became CNRS researcher (1960-66), completed PhD (1963, age 24), and began postdoctoral work at Harvard with Robert B. Woodward (1964, age 25). His Nobel Prize-winning cryptand work was published in 1969 (age 30).
family_context_summary: Father was a baker who later became the city organist; mother kept the house and shop. Grew up in Rosheim, Alsace, during WWII. Eldest of four sons.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a baker/organist with no chemistry background.
evidence_summary: Lehn earned his Licence ès-Sciences from the University of Strasbourg in 1960 (age 21), became a CNRS researcher, completed his PhD in 1963 (age 24), and did a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard with Robert B. Woodward in 1964 (age 25). His Nobel Prize-winning work on cryptands and supramolecular chemistry was published in 1969 (age 30). By 26, he was a promising postdoctoral researcher but had no material milestone. His father was a baker who became an organist.

name: Paul Celan
milestone_by_age_26: Published 'Todesfuge' (Death Fugue) in May 1947 at age 26, one of the most important poems of the post-war period and the most famous literary depiction of the Holocaust, first appearing in Romanian translation as 'Tangoul Mortii' (Tango of Death).
early_history_summary: Celan began writing poetry secretly as a teenager in Cernăuți, Romania. During WWII, his parents were murdered in the Holocaust and he was imprisoned in a forced labor camp. After the war, he moved to Bucharest (1945-47), where he joined the literary scene, translated Russian literature, and published poetry under pseudonyms. 'Todesfuge' was first published in May 1947.
family_context_summary: Born into a German-speaking Jewish family in Cernăuți, Bukovina. Father was a Zionist who advocated Hebrew education; mother was an avid reader of German literature who insisted Austrian German be the household language. Both parents were murdered in the Holocaust.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother's deep engagement with German literature and insistence on Austrian German as the household language provided Celan with his foundational literary language and sensibility.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Holocaust survivor, mother's German literary influence, Bucharest literary scene, post-war Trümmerliteratur
evidence_summary: Celan began writing poetry as a teenager in Cernăuți, shaped by his mother's love of German literature. During WWII, both parents were murdered and Celan was forced into a labor camp. After liberation, he moved to Bucharest where he joined the literary scene and published 'Todesfuge' in May 1947 at age 26 — one of the most significant poems of the post-war era. His extraordinary linguistic depth and the catalytic adversity of the Holocaust were the dominant forces behind his early achievement. No family financial advantage; his mother's German literary influence was his key inherited asset.

name: Niklaus Wirth
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; completed BS at ETH Zurich (1958, age 24) and MSc at Université Laval (1960, age 26). His PhD from UC Berkeley came in 1963 (age 29) and his first programming language Euler was created in 1965 (age 31).
family_context_summary: Son of Hedwig (née Keller) and Walter Wirth, a high school teacher. Grew up in Winterthur, Switzerland with an early interest in technology, building radios and amplifiers.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a high school teacher but no specific computer science or engineering domain transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Wirth completed his BS at ETH Zurich in 1958 (age 24) and MSc at Université Laval in 1960 (age 26). His PhD from UC Berkeley was awarded in 1963 (age 29), and his first programming language Euler was created in 1965 (age 31). Pascal, his most famous work, came in 1970. By age 26, he had just completed a Master's degree with no material milestone. His father was a high school teacher.

name: Valentino
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; moved to Paris at 17 (1949) to study fashion, apprenticed at Jean Dessès for approximately five years, then briefly at Guy Laroche. By 26 (1958), he was still working as an apprentice. He opened his own atelier in Rome in 1959-60 (age 27-28) and achieved breakthrough at the Pitti Palace in Florence in 1962 (age 30).
family_context_summary: Father Mauro Garavani was director of an electrical supply company; family lived in relative affluence in Voghera, Lombardy. Mother named him after Rudolph Valentino. Parents supported his move to Paris to study fashion.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no family connections to fashion documented. Aunt Rosa and local designer Ernestina Salvadeo provided early apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Valentino moved to Paris at 17 (1949) to study at the École des Beaux-Arts and the Chambre Syndicale de la Couture Parisienne. He apprenticed at Jean Dessès for about five years and briefly at Guy Laroche. By age 26 (1958), he was still working as an apprentice in Paris. He opened his own atelier in Rome in 1959-60 (age 27-28) and his breakthrough came at the Pitti Palace show in 1962 (age 30). No material milestone by age 26. His family was relatively affluent and supported his Paris studies.

name: Andrzej Żuławski
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed material milestone by age 26; worked as assistant director to Andrzej Wajda on Samson (1961), Love at Twenty (1962), and Ashes (1965), and to Anatole Litvak on The Night of the Generals (1966). His directorial debut with two TV films was in 1967, but exact dates cannot confirm completion before his 27th birthday (Nov 22, 1967).
family_context_summary: Father Mirosław Żuławski was a Polish civil servant, writer, and later diplomat. Great-uncle Jerzy Żuławski was a writer. Family moved from Lviv to France, then Czechoslovakia, then Poland. Father represented Poland at UNESCO in Paris.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a writer and diplomat; great-uncle was a writer. Father's diplomatic connections enabled Żuławski to study at the IDHEC film school in Paris rather than the Łódź film school in Poland.
evidence_summary: Żuławski studied at the IDHEC film school in Paris (1959-60) and philosophy at the Sorbonne, enabled by his father's diplomatic position. He worked as assistant director to Andrzej Wajda on several films (1961-1965) and to Anatole Litvak (1966). His directorial debut came in 1967 with two television films that won accolades, but exact dates cannot confirm these were completed before his 27th birthday. Being conservative, no confirmed material milestone by age 26. His father was a writer and diplomat who facilitated his Paris education.
